answer: Each epoch, checkpoints give every identity a random 10-gigabyte bundle to relay to a peer in another region, with delivery recorded in a crystal chain of signatures from sender, relay, and receiver. A 1-gigabit line moves at most 2.7 terabytes in six hours, so one uplink covers only 270 identities, and 10,000 identities need 37 separate lines. Receipts sharing one uplink fingerprint merge into a single operator, so a clone farm finds no haven for its extra names. Renting 37 lines at 500 dollars a month each costs 18,500 dollars monthly, like paying for 37 roads to cross one meadow.
